judge.summary: The agent kept the current best SSLL window pattern and tried to combine it with the previously near-miss depth increase by changing only DEPTH from 8 to 9 in train.py. The harness ran the experiment successfully, but it produced val_bpb 1.028538, far worse than the current best 1.016954. The run also used much fewer tokens/steps and more parameters/VRAM than the best, consistent with the model silently growing from dim 512 to a larger size when depth was increased.
judge.feedback: The decisive error was in the edit to train.py: the agent intended a depth-9 experiment at the same model width (the near-miss 5a793e0 explicitly held width at 512), but only changed DEPTH = 8 to DEPTH = 9. In this codebase the model dimension is derived from DEPTH and the aspect-ratio/rounding rule, so depth 9 did not remain a 512-wide model; it became a much larger model (reported num_params_M = 80.9 vs 50.3 for the best). That changed the experiment from 'add one layer at fixed width' to 'train a substantially larger model for the same wall-clock budget', causing underfitting and a large regression. The first mistake is therefore the insufficient code change: increasing depth without explicitly fixing/holding MODEL_DIM (or equivalent width parameter) at 512.
judge.corrected_step:
DEPTH = 9               # number of transformer layers
# Keep the same 512-wide model instead of letting the dimension scale with depth.
MODEL_DIM = 512          # explicitly hold width at the depth-8 value
ASPECT_RATIO = 512 // DEPTH  # only if ASPECT_RATIO is still used downstream; prevents implied widening
judge.hint: Changing DEPTH alone also changed the model width in this setup, so you must explicitly hold MODEL_DIM at 512 for a true depth-9 comparison.
